title: The Universe and the Solar System
seo_title: Earth and Space Science 1: The Universe and the Solar System Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)
standard_code: Earth and Space Science 1, Quarter 1: Origin and Structure of the Earth
standard_text: Composition of the universe; the big bang; stars and galaxies; the origin of the solar system; Earth's position within the solar system and the conditions that make it habitable. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Earth and Space Science 1, Quarter 1)
meta_desc: Free Earth and Space Science 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 1): the big bang, stars and galaxies, the origin of the solar system and Earth's place in it. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The universe began with the big bang about 13.8 billion years ago.
key_sub: The solar system formed from a nebula about 4.6 billion years ago.
body_html:
How to think about it

The big bang theory says the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since; evidence includes the red shift of galaxies and the cosmic microwave background. Stars form in clouds of gas and dust, fuse hydrogen into helium, and make heavier elements.

The solar system formed about 4.6 billion years ago from a spinning nebula: the Sun formed at the center and the planets formed from the disk. Rocky planets formed near the Sun and gas giants farther out. Earth's distance from the Sun lets water stay liquid.

Example

Which evidence shows the universe is expanding?

Light from galaxies

Answer: the red shift of distant galaxies

Example

Why are the inner planets rocky?

Hot near the Sun

Answer: only rock and metal could condense close to the Sun

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the big bang was an explosion in space.
  • Thinking all stars are the same age.
  • Thinking planets formed before the Sun.
